relevance_note: A 26-patient inborn-errors-of-immunity cohort in which exactly one patient carries a TNFAIP3 variant: 'TNFAIP3 (P22)', 'TNFAIP3:c.2152del(40m)'.
method_note: Read the full Markdown by hand; values were typed into a small Python builder script and every span was checked by script against the paper. SCOPE: the cohort has 26 IEI patients with variants in 11 genes; only P22 (the single TNFAIP3 carrier) was extracted, because the study is about TNFAIP3/HA20 and the instructions leave tables empty for non-TNFAIP3 patients. The other 25 patients (CD40LG, STAT3, RAG1/2, IL2RG, CTLA4, SH2D1A, FAS, DOCK8, FOXP3) were deliberately not extracted. P22 is identified as the TNFAIP3 patient from 'TNFAIP3 (P22)' and Table 1; the Discussion and Autoantibody sections refer to 'one patient with a TNFAIP3 mutation' without a label, which was attributed to P22 because the paper reports only one TNFAIP3 patient. The paper never uses the term 'A20 haploinsufficiency' or 'HA20' for P22 (only in reference titles); disease label records IEI plus type 1 diabetes. Table 1 'Age at onset (month)' value '40' is recorded as printed, with the unit taken from the column header for the ISO conversion; the 'Mutation (Age atdiagnosis)' cell reads 'TNFAIP3:c.2152del(40m)Hypergly' (the trailing 'Hypergly' looks like a conversion artifact); '40m' recorded as age at (genetic) diagnosis. Hyperglycemia onset '40' is inferred from the row's onset age plus 'Initial symptom' column. Empty Table 1 cells (Infection, Digestive symptom, Lymphoproliferative) treated as not reported. Recurrent infections excluded from the Discussion statement 'without recurrent infections' despite 'Anti-infection prophylaxis' therapy. Autoantibodies: routine (conventional ELISA/IFA) autoantibody tests were negative for P22, while the research antigen microarray (threshold: >=3-fold NFI vs 9 healthy controls) showed elevated autoantibodies including anti-IA2; both rows emitted, checklist 'autoantibodies (ANA/other)' set observed on the microarray result (assay-specific, not treated as a contradiction). Skin lesions checklist observed from 'Eczema'. Ethnicity 'Chinese' from the cohort-wide statement covering all 26 patients. Pathogenicity 'pathogenic mutations' comes from a cohort-wide sentence, not a variant-specific classification. Variant type, transcript, protein change, inheritance and parental testing not reported. CONTRADICTIONS in the paper (not P22-specific rows): Results say P4 and P22 had clinical autoimmunity with negative routine autoantibody tests, but the Discussion says the 'nine patients' with microarray-only positivity 'exhibited no overt autoimmune symptoms'; cohort autoimmunity is given as 8 (30.8%) patients but also 'five patients presented with clinical manifestations of autoimmunity' and '10 patients did not present with clinical manifestations'; 'ten distinct immunodeficiency-related genes' while 11 gene symbols are listed. Supplementary Tables S1-S4 (autoantibody and immunology data per patient) are not in the converted text.
